problem_summary.summary: Starting at index zero, determine whether the final array index can be reached when each value gives the maximum forward jump from that position.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: non-empty nums of maximum jump lengths. Return whether index nums.length - 1 is reachable.

brute_force.explanation: Use a boolean reachability table. From each reachable index, mark every position within its allowed jump range.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The table marks exactly positions reachable by a legal final jump from an already reachable position; induction from index zero covers every possible path.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) worst case — many reachable indices may mark long overlapping ranges.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) — one reachability flag is stored per index.

optimized.explanation: Track the farthest index reachable from any position scanned so far. If the scan reaches beyond that boundary, the last index is unreachable.
optimized.correctness_idea: Every scanned index at or before farthest is reachable. Extending farthest with index + nums[index] includes all positions reachable through that index; a gap past the boundary cannot be crossed.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — indices are scanned at most once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only the farthest reachable index is maintained.

steps.action: Extend the reachable boundary to index 2.

steps.condition: 2 <= current farthest 2 and index + nums[index] = 4 reaches the last index.
steps.action: Extend farthest to 4 and return true.

edge_cases.handling: The starting position is already the final position.
If the farthest boundary ends before the last index, the next index beyond it causes false.

edge_cases.case: A jump reaches or passes the last index
edge_cases.handling: The method returns true as soon as farthest reaches the goal.
